suggestions.rationale: Mapping Expansion Batch ME-32 adds this relationship only as a bounded same-joint degenerative association. The International Ankle Consortium evidence review associates recurrent lateral ankle sprains and chronic ankle instability with increasing rates of post-traumatic ankle osteoarthritis in the injured ankle, but the primary diagnosis alone does not establish osteoarthritis in every person or determine an individual's degenerative course. Require independently documented ankle sprain with documented chronic instability or recurrent injury, radiographically documented ipsilateral ankle osteoarthritis compatible in chronology, and orthopedic review. Preserve prior ankle fracture, talar osteochondral lesion, malalignment, inflammatory arthropathy, and other competing causes of ankle degeneration.
evidenceGaps: Independent documentation of ankle sprain injury with recurrent episodes or chronic instability
Radiographic documentation of ipsilateral ankle osteoarthritis with compatible chronology
Assessment of prior fracture, osteochondral lesion, and malalignment
Assessment of inflammatory arthropathy and other degenerative alternatives
Orthopedic assessment distinguishing sprain-related degeneration from other causes

sourceReferences.note: International Ankle Consortium evidence review associating recurrent lateral ankle sprains and chronic ankle instability with increasing rates of post-traumatic ankle osteoarthritis. It supports a bounded disease-association proposition and clinical evaluation, not automatic individual causation or aggravation.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Recurrent lateral ankle sprains and chronic ankle instability are associated with increased rates of post-traumatic ankle osteoarthritis in the injured joint, but population-level association evidence does not establish an individual medical nexus without documentation of both the injury history and the degenerative disease, compatible chronology, and competing-cause review.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation under 38 CFR § 3.310 is established by this association evidence; the mapping is not an individual nexus opinion.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: Repetitive inversion injury with ligamentous laxity is hypothesized to alter tibiotalar joint loading and articular contact mechanics, promoting cartilage wear, but the individual pathway must be established from imaging, instability history, and orthopedic evaluation.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: This relationship is supported as an association only. Chronic ankle instability is associated with post-traumatic ankle osteoarthritis in consortium review evidence, but that evidence does not establish that ankle sprains caused or aggravated osteoarthritis in every individual; both diagnoses, chronology, imaging findings, and competing etiologies require case-specific review.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Documented sprain history and osteoarthritis; chronology; weight-bearing imaging; fracture, osteochondral, malalignment, and inflammatory alternatives; orthopedic assessment of the individual relationship
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Prior ankle fracture or talar osteochondral injury
Inflammatory arthropathy or primary degenerative disease of independent etiology
